سَفِيفٌ Woven [with the fingers, or plaited,] of palm-leaves. (KL.) ―
-b2- [And hence,] The girth of the رَحْل [or camel's saddle], (S, M, K,) and of the [women's vehicle called] هَوْدَج: (M:) the fore-girth of the رَحْل; because made broad, like the سَفِيف of palm-leaves. (T, TA.) [See also the next paragraph.] ＝
-A2- A certain plant. (IDrd, K.) ＝
-A3- The sharpness of the ears of the wolf. (M, TA.) ＝
-A4- And السَّفِيفُ is A name of Iblees: (O, K:) so says AA: (O:) in one or more of the copies of the “ Nawádir, ” ↓ السَّفْسَفُ . (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
